source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Aurora campus publishes 114 MW of IT capacity, making it the largest single disclosed facility in Illinois and representing 48 percent of the state's published data center power.

At 114 MW and assuming conservative mixed-workload density, the campus could host roughly 2,280 H100 GPUs if fully deployed for AI training. The actual number depends on tenant mix, which the operator does not disclose. This capacity is material but insufficient for the largest training clusters, which typically require colocation of multiple facilities or dedicated infrastructure.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities, but only six publish capacity figures. The remaining 38 facilities report no power metrics, meaning actual state capacity is substantially higher than the 236 MW of published figures. The Aurora campus dominates disclosed capacity, but this reflects reporting opacity rather than technical dominance.

The campus matters to AI infrastructure primarily as a local constraint on the Chicago metro region. Whether it becomes central to AI scaling depends on three unknowns the data does not cover: total grid supply available to the site, what fraction of the 114 MW the operator allocates to AI versus other workloads, and whether CyrusOne publishes additional capacity figures that are not yet sourced.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
